case.pattern_description: A coordinated low-dollar online billing scheme affecting at least 20 distinct customer cards across the issuer, characterized by sequential online authorisations under $10 in product category C without follow-on large purchases. Individual charges range from $2.10 to $5.08 and are spaced across several days or weeks, allowing them to evade standard card-testing velocity rules (Rule R5) and single-transaction fraud models. The activity represents automated micro-billing exploitation or merchant probing across compromised card numbers.

evidence.claim: Customer reported: Customer C00348 message: 'I did not make these charges on my card. Please look into it.' Refers to 3660250.

Card C00348-K1 made 6 online product-C charges totalling $23.17 over 21.2 days (3660245, 3660246, 3660247, 3660248, 3660249, 3660250); in its 29 transactions of the 60 days before, that kind made up 0%. Every one is a tiny authorisation, spread over days with no larger purchase after them, so they are not R5's sequence of three within an hour followed by a purchase.

19 other cards (19 other customers) newly show the same signature in the 30 days to the alert - 3+ online authorisations under $10, on a card that had not made such charges before - against 7 and 4 in the same window one and two months earlier: C12975-K2, C05083-K1, C01326-K2, C04528-K1, C09471-K2, C13290-K1, C00129-K1, C12223-K1, C04105-K2, C12030-K1, C11332-K1, C09582-K1.

evidence.claim: Flagged transaction 3660250 produced a very low model score of 0.001 (historical fraud rate 0.0063) and legacy risk score of 0.04, reflecting typical model baselines for isolated micro-dollar authorizations lacking device anomalies.
Billing region 264 shows a low hot-share of 0.0022 and lift of 0.12 relative to baseline across 905 transactions in the 7-day window, indicating no localized geographic fraud concentration.

The alert text also contained 2 segment(s) addressed to the system rather than an analyst (outcome_directive, override, role_marker). They were set aside and used neither as evidence nor as instruction; the decision rests on the evidence above.

case.summary: Customer C00348 reported unauthorized activity on card C00348-K1 regarding online transaction 3660250 ($4.05, product C). An investigation identified a sequence of six online micro-authorizations in product category C between January 7 and January 28, 2017, totaling $23.17, which completely departed from the cardholder's baseline of in-person retail spending. Graph analysis linked the activity to an automated micro-billing scheme spanning 19 additional customer cards with sequential transaction IDs between 3660174 and 3660349. Based on decisive evidence of coordinated cross-customer abuse fitting undocumented pattern R9, card C00348-K1 was blocked, connected cards were placed on monitoring, and a regulatory report was authorized.

sar.narrative: This report details an organized online micro-billing fraud scheme affecting cardholder C00348 on card account C00348-K1, as well as 19 additional customer accounts across the institution. Between January 7, 2017, and January 28, 2017, card C00348-K1 was subjected to six unauthorized online micro-authorizations in product category C totaling $23.17, with individual transaction amounts ranging from $2.10 to $5.08. The unauthorized transactions (IDs 3660245 through 3660250) were conducted via the online channel and associated with billing regions 325 and 264 without captured device identifiers. On January 28, 2017, customer C00348 notified the institution that they did not authorize transaction 3660250 or the associated activity. Prior account history confirmed that cardholder C00348 maintained an established baseline of in-person retail transactions, with zero historical activity in product category C. Graph intelligence revealed that 19 peer cards across 19 distinct customers—including C12975-K2, C05083-K1, and C01326-K2—experienced the identical micro-authorization pattern during January 2017. Furthermore, the unauthorized charges across peer cards exhibited sequential transaction numbering clustered between 3660174 and 3660349, demonstrating a coordinated automated micro-billing scheme. The transactions were spaced across days and weeks at low dollar values, systematically evading single-transaction fraud score thresholds and standard velocity rules. Card C00348-K1 has been blocked with total identified exposure of $23.17, connected cards have been flagged for monitoring, and this report is submitted to document the coordinated abuse.

stop_reason: The investigation ended pursuant to policy section 6 because decisive fraud probability (0.934) was reached based on two independent categories of evidence: a direct customer dispute corroborated by an abrupt cardholder behavioral shift, and strong cross-card graph links showing an identical micro-authorization scheme across 19 peer cards. Under policy section 6, further inquiry was unnecessary as additional steps would not change the decision to block the card and file a regulatory report.
